ops.description:
Found 2026-08-16 while converging two machines from 0.65.0 to 0.65.2 (the Trust.Control fix,
note 28633ad). Distinct from that bug — it appears only AFTER the trust fix lets the install
get far enough to supersede.

Repro on both machines:
1. Machine has 0.65.0 installed, ~/.cc-pool/fusekit/catalog.sqlite written by its runtime.
2. brew upgrade cc-pool to 0.65.2.
3. launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.yasyf.cc-pool.status.fusekit  (needed because the
   0.65.0 daemon refuses the drain — that is the trust bug).
4. ccp package install

The app installs and activation.json seals correctly, then the install fails:

    require the live FuseKit runtime: daemonkit: no daemon is listening:
    wire: dial: dial unix ~/com.yasyf.cc-pool.tenants/daemon.sock: connect: no such file or directory

Because the new runtime never comes up. ~/.cc-pool/fusekit/holder.log fills with, unbounded:

    CCPoolStatus: FuseKit runtime start failed: publish exact source fleet:
    catalog: tenant generation mismatch: catalog: tenant generation mismatch

Both LaunchAgents end at launchctl status 1, the fusekit one with no PID.

Workaround (what I did): stop both agents, `rm -rf ~/.cc-pool/fusekit`, then
`ccp package install && ccp init`. Both machines then reach
"✓ Daemon and FuseKit runtime are ready (v0.65.2)" with status 0 and a sealed activation.json.
pool-v1.db is not involved and was not touched — accounts survive this.

Why it needs a real fix: there is no self-healing and no actionable error. The user sees a
dial failure naming a socket, while the actual cause is a persisted catalog generation, in a
different file, reported only in a log they have no reason to open. Both machines here had
zero accounts so deletion was free; on a populated pool the same wedge is a support incident.

Second, smaller issue seen during the same converge: `rm -rf ~/.cc-pool/fusekit` immediately
after a successful `launchctl bootout` failed with "Directory not empty" — the runtime was
still writing processes.db after bootout returned. Whatever performs this cleanup needs to
wait for the process to actually exit, not just for bootout to return.

--- CORRECTION 2026-08-17 ---

Reading the code behind this changed the diagnosis. The root cause is cc-pool's own, not
fusekit's, and it is not upgrade-specific.

claudeSourceFleetPublication (internal/tenantfs/source_fleet.go:39) builds every
publication with a hardcoded ExpectedGeneration: 0 while publishing
Generation: SourceAuthorityFleetGeneration, which is 1 (internal/tenantfs/source_fleet.go:54-58,
the constant at internal/tenantfs/driver_factories.go:19). That pair is a compare-and-swap
precondition, and it only holds against a catalog that has never seen this owner. fusekit's
ReconcileSourceAuthorityFleet refuses on

    case currentFound && current.Generation != request.ExpectedGeneration:
        return SourceAuthorityFleetReconcileState{}, ErrGenerationMismatch

(fusekit v1.16.1, the version go.mod pins — catalog/source_authority_fleet.go:701-706). So
after one successful publish the stored generation is 1, the request still expects 0, and
the precondition can never hold again.

startHolder calls PublishClaudeSourceFleet on EVERY runtime start
(cmd/cc-pool-runtime-archive/main.go:87, the func at :78). It is not gated on first install,
on an empty catalog, or on anything else. So the wedge fires on the first restart after a
successful publish.

SEVERITY CORRECTION: this is NOT upgrade-specific, and the title's framing of it as a 0.65.0
catalog crash-looping a 0.65.2 runtime is wrong.

    git diff v0.65.0..v0.65.2 -- internal/tenantfs/source_fleet.go cmd/cc-pool-runtime-archive/main.go

is empty — run 2026-08-17, zero bytes of output, exit 0. Neither the publication nor its call
site moved between those two tags; the whole v0.65.0..v0.65.2 Go diff is
internal/holderbridge/plan.go and its test, the trust fix of note 28633ad. Both files are also
unchanged from v0.65.2 to HEAD. The upgrade was merely the first restart. A plain reboot fires
the identical wedge, so every machine that has published the fleet is still exposed — and by
the same code, the recorded workaround (rm -rf ~/.cc-pool/fusekit) clears the catalog and buys
exactly one more clean start before the mismatch returns.

The restart path is untested, and the existing test actively pins the broken precondition:
TestClaudeSourceFleetPublicationIsExactV1Topology (internal/tenantfs/source_fleet_test.go:9)
asserts at line 14 that publication.ExpectedGeneration != 0 is a failure. A fix has to change
that assertion, not just the publication.

The second issue above — rm -rf ~/.cc-pool/fusekit failing with "Directory not empty" straight
after a successful launchctl bootout — is a CONSEQUENCE of the trust bug (note 28633ad), not an
independent defect. daemonkit's own Client.Stop already proves the process gone before it
touches launchd: "The LaunchAgent goes last, after departure is proven, so launchd never
relaunches what was just drained" (daemonkit/stop.go:41-43), and its body loops stopOnce to a
proof of departure before removeAgent runs at all (daemonkit/stop.go:77-96). The race appeared
only because every daemonkit stop path was gated on the refused control lane, leaving raw
launchctl as the only lever. The residual daemonkit gap this exposed — launchd.Remove called
directly boots out without waiting — is filed as daemonkit task 5f373d3; the missing actionable
error this bug asks for is daemonkit task 0cdd5b2.
